chunks: We had assigned to them close companions who made their past and present look attractive to them; and the fate that had once befallen the communities of jinns and men before them was justified upon them. They were indeed bound to perish.

key_terms.بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ: What is in front of them (future/worldly life)
key_terms.حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ: The decree/fate was justified upon them
key_terms.قُرَنَاءَ: Close companions or devils assigned to mislead

ai.seo_question: Who are the Quranah mentioned in the Quran and how do they mislead humans?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the mechanism of divine punishment where 'quranah' (often interpreted as devils or evil companions) embellish the sins of the disbelievers, leading to their spiritual blindness. It underscores the concept of 'haqq al-qawl' (the fulfillment of the decree), indicating that their destruction was a just consequence of their own choices, mirroring the fate of previous generations of jinn and humans. This serves as a practical warning that external temptations are internalized through one's own acceptance, making the decree of loss inevitable.
